diagnostic_question: Is the suspected leak/invalid free real, or a false positive / benign report?
What does the tool's report category or runtime error mean (definitely/indirectly/possibly lost, still reachable, suppressed, invalid pointer)?
Is the report caused by my code, or by a library, runtime, or the tool itself?
Where was the block allocated / where does the leak or bad free originate?
How do I detect, configure, or suppress this with the tool?
Is this memory on the heap at all (vs. stack, static, string literal)?
Does this function/API allocate what it returns (must the caller free it)?
Which allocator family produced this pointer (malloc/new/new[]/custom/library)?
Is the allocation size bounded and validated (untrusted input, overflow, huge/negative size, failure)?
Who is responsible for releasing this memory (caller vs. callee contract)?
Was ownership transferred (to a container, smart pointer, library, or object), so someone else releases it?
Is there a matching release for this allocation, and where should it go?
Is the pointer passed to free exactly the one the allocator returned (not offset/advanced)?
Is the deallocator the right one for the allocator (free vs delete vs delete[] vs library free)?
Is the pointer valid to free right now (initialized, not already freed, not dangling)?
Is the memory released on every path: error handling, early return, exceptions, longjmp?
Is the old block released on each loop iteration / reallocation (realloc failure, reassignment in a loop)?
Must the memory be freed before program exit, or is exit-time retention acceptable?
Is the object destroyed when its lifetime ends (scope exit, destructor called, virtual destructor)?
Does memory keep growing with repetitions (retained longer than needed, unbounded growth)?
Are threads joined/detached so that their resources are released?
Was the last reference overwritten or lost before release?
Does the pointer escape (global, struct field, return value) so it must be released elsewhere?
Do other aliases or copies refer to the same block (shallow copy, copy ctor, two owners)?
Are nested sub-allocations released (struct members, list nodes, 2-D arrays) before/with the parent?
Is a reference cycle or refcount imbalance preventing release?
Does the cleanup routine / destructor release every resource the object owns?
Are allocation and release done by the same module/runtime heap (DLL, CRT, FFI boundary)?
Generic: why does this leak/crash? (no specific evidence asked)
Triage: reproducer, full trace, version, build flags
Prevention / best-practice advice
Allocator internals (how free knows the size, etc.)
